title: Imaging Mass Cytometer Tuning
author: Michelle Daniel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf2gjqbw
materials: Hit “New” to create a new tuning template.

steps.title: Check recent tuning date
steps.instruction: If the instrument is running, open the file “tuning log sheet.ods”, note the date of the last tuning, and if it was performed more than two days ago continue with the next steps.

steps.title: Verify argon supply
steps.instruction: Check argon pressure (5 bar) and ensure at least one argon tank is ≥25 % full (sufficient for overnight use). If a tank is insufficient, obtain a new tank from the basement shop using the PanGas pay card.

steps.title: Verify helium supply
steps.instruction: Check helium pressure (2 bar) and inspect the helium bottles in the cabinet. If pressure falls below 100 bar, open the second bottle, close the empty one, move the empty bottle to the front of the room, hang a sign “Empty”, and inform Esther Danenberg or Stefanie Engler to order a replacement.

steps.title: Launch CyTOF software
steps.instruction: Open the CyTOF software on the computer and log in with your user name and password.

steps.title: Insert tuning slide
steps.instruction: Place the tuning slide into the Hyperion instrument.

steps.title: Start plasma and equilibrate
steps.instruction: Start the plasma and allow the system to equilibrate for at least 30 minutes before proceeding with tuning.

steps.title: Adjust laser E‑ref
steps.instruction: Perform laser E‑ref adjustment and record values as follows:

substeps.instruction: Confirm that “Adjust E‑ref” needs to be performed; if not, skip to auto‑tune.
Click “Settings” under Manual Tune.
In the camera window, move to an empty region next to an ablated region on the right side.
Press “Get Current Coordinate” in the Manual Tune Settings.
Copy the displayed Ablation Energy Range values to the tuning log sheet.
Click “Adjust Eref”.
Copy the new Ablation Energy Range values to the tuning log sheet.
Note: This adjustment should be repeated every 2–3 weeks; check the tuning log sheet on the IMC computer for the last performance date.

steps.title: Run auto‑tune
steps.instruction: Execute the instrument auto‑tune routine and record results:

substeps.instruction: Click “Auto Tune” under Instrument Control.
Select “New” to create a new tuning template.
In the camera window, move to an empty space next to previously ablated regions on the right side.
Press “Get Current Coordinate” in the Auto Tune window.
Under Parameters, enable “QC Report”, “HTI Current/Gases Calibration”, and “Transient Calibration”.
Click “Run”.
If the tuning fails, repeat the run once with the same parameters.
If it fails again, also enable “Coarse XY Optimization” and “Fine XY Optimization” and run.
If tuning still fails, contact Daniel Schulz, Esther Danenberg, or Stefanie Engler. (XY optimization is only required if the torch box has been opened or tuning continuously fails.)

steps.title: Validate tuning results
steps.instruction: Check the tuning outcome and log all parameters:

substeps.instruction: If the tuning passes, verify that the Transient Cross Talk value is < 0.05; if higher, the Hyperion and Helios are mis‑aligned – align tubing or contact Esther Danenberg, Stefanie Engler, or Daniel Schulz for assistance.
Compare the detector voltage to previous tuning records; jumps greater than 50 V indicate possible detector deterioration – contact Daniel Schulz.
Copy all required parameters from the Results window into the tuning log sheet on the IMC computer.
